attacks.attack: 1. Forge the quorum with the operator's own keys
attacks.detail: k operator-signed anchors claiming registry ids -> valid=[], witnessed=False. The operator cannot mint witnesses with keys it controls.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — pinned-key match rejects operator-minted witnesses

attacks.attack: 2. Replay a witness cosignature onto a rewritten root
attacks.detail: witness-0's cosig over R transplanted onto R' -> valid=[], witnessed=False. The cosignature covers the root, so it won't verify on R'.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — a cosignature binds the exact root

attacks.attack: 3. >= k colluding witnesses witness a forged root
attacks.detail: 3 genuine witnesses co-sign a forged root -> witnessed=True. Quorum defends up to (k-1) dishonest witnesses; at k it falls. k/n + independence + who-pays-without-recentralizing is the economic question (G3), not solved here.
attacks.verdict: ACCEPTED LIMIT — at >= k collusion a lie can be witnessed (gate G3)

attacks.detail: witness-0 cosigns both R and R' at the same (log_id, tree_size) -> conflicts=1. Comparing statements reveals the fork regardless of who signed.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — equivocation is caught even with a single witness

attacks.detail: over-claim hits: none; discloses collusion/G3: True; discloses liveness: True.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — discloses the >=k-collusion and liveness limits
